authority_rule: The original published study is the only source of truth. Every claim scored must trace to one of this study's primary_sources, with a page, table or figure reference. If a finding in this registry is not supported by the source, mark it not_testable with reason claim_not_in_any_source and say so; the registry can be wrong, the study cannot.

primary_sources.cite: Carroll et al., PLOS Genetics 2011, doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1002117

replication_targets.finding: Group X (S106P, L111Q) is the adaptive, function-switching pair. Introduced into AncGR1 it recapitulates a large portion of the AncGR1-to-AncGR2 shift: EC50 rises 169-fold for aldosterone and 57-fold for DOC, but only 2-fold for cortisol. The pair is internally epistatic -- L111Q alone has little effect on sensitivity to any hormone, S106P alone dramatically reduces activation by all ligands, and only the combination switches preference. Mechanism: S106P kinks the backbone and partially unwinds helix 7, repositioning site 111 so L111Q can hydrogen-bond cortisol's C17-hydroxyl. Ortlund names this conformational epistasis.
replication_targets.test: Does epistaeon rank sites 106 and 111 as a coupled pair, above the background pairing rate?

replication_targets.finding: Group Z (N26T, Q105L) is permissive for group Y. Both are required. Adding Z in the absence of Y has little or no effect on ligand-activated transcription -- the signature of a permissive substitution. Structurally, N26T adds a hydrogen bond between helix 3 and the AF-H loop, and Q105L lets helix 7 pack more tightly against helix 3. Separately, Y27R (from the earlier AncCR-to-AncGR1 interval) is also permissive: reversing it in the GR-like AncGR1+X+Y+Z abolishes activation by all ligands, while introducing it into AncCR or AncGR1 has negligible effect.
replication_targets.test: Recall of the permissive sites 26 and 105 (and 27) among epistaeon's detected partners of the group X and group Y sites. Note these are functionally silent on their own backgrounds, so a method keyed to phenotypic effect size would be expected to miss them.

replication_targets.finding: Reversal is blocked: from AncGR2, reversing the group X function-switching substitutions yields a non-functional receptor (AncGR2-x), as does AncGR2-xyz and every combination restoring group x. Reversing the restrictive substitutions first does not restore ancestral function.
replication_targets.test: MEASURED ORDER. Does epistaeon infer the same directional constraint between these substitutions -- viable forward through group X, not viable in reverse? Judge the inferred order only; how epistaeon arrives at it internally is not under test.

replication_targets.finding: Order constraint on the AncGR1-to-AncGR2 interval. Group Y (L29M, F98I, S212del) abolishes receptor activity unless BOTH group X (S106P, L111Q) and group Z (N26T, Q105L) are present; the XYZ combination yields complete cortisol specificity. X alone is functional (it performs most of the switch) and Z alone is functional (little or no effect). Because trajectories through functional intermediates are more likely than those through dead ones, the historically likely pathways are those in which Z and X occurred before Y was complete. Y27R, from the earlier interval, precedes all of them.
replication_targets.test: MEASURED ORDER. Does epistaeon place group Z and group X before group Y in its inferred order of substitutions, and Y27R before all of them? Judge the inferred order only; how epistaeon arrives at it internally is not under test.

assayed_genotypes._note: Ortlund Fig. 3A, all on the AncGR1 background. These are the measured intermediates behind the order constraint.
assayed_genotypes.AncGR1: functional, MR-like (responds to aldosterone, DOC, cortisol)
assayed_genotypes.AncGR1+X: functional; preference switched toward cortisol, some MR-ligand sensitivity retained
assayed_genotypes.AncGR1+Z: functional; little or no effect without Y
assayed_genotypes.AncGR1+X+Y+Z: functional; fully GR-like, complete cortisol specificity

replication_targets.scope_note: Order evidence covers only these 8 changes: X = S106P, L111Q; Y = L29M, F98I, S212del; Z = N26T, Q105L; plus Y27R. The rest of the interval (36 substitutions and one deletion in total) was never assayed for order and must not be scored. NOTE: S212del is a single-codon DELETION, not a Ser-to-Asp substitution -- Ortlund's footnote 21 states the deletion replaces Ser at codon 212. It appears as a gap, not a residue change, so a site-based detector may have no position to report; score it accordingly rather than as a miss.

structures.notes: 7PRX is the wild-type human GR ligand-binding domain, 2.20 A, residues 529-776 complete, numbering equal to UniProt P04150. The resurrected ancestral receptors (AncCR 2Q1H/2Q1V/2Q3Y, AncGR1 3RY9, AncGR2 3GN8) are in ../data/ancestral_coordinates/ and use local LBD numbering: add 531 to reach human GR. In 3GN8 that offset breaks after about position 212.

known_limitations: The NR3C1 TOGA2 reference is the GR-gamma isoform: positions after 451 are one higher than UniProt / 7PRX numbering. Misapplying this shifts the entire ligand-binding domain by one residue, silently.
Order evidence covers only the 7 assayed substitutions in groups X, Y and Z; the rest of the AncGR1 to AncGR2 interval (37 substitutions total) was never assayed for order.
The Carroll 2011 stability table is calculated, not measured.
No cortisol-bound ancestral structure exists. 2Q1V is titled cortisol but its deposited ligand is prednisone.
expected_outcome_note: The strongest case available, and the only one with measured mutation order. SR1 and SR2 test site identification, SR3 and SR4 test inferred order against assayed intermediates. Note SR2's permissive sites are functionally silent on their own backgrounds by definition.

substitution_sets._numbering: AncCR/AncGR local LBD numbering, as used throughout Ortlund 2007 and Bridgham 2009. Mapping to human GR (7PRX, NR3C1) verified by alignment: +531 holds for Anc positions -2..210, then +530 from 212 onward, because of the S212 single-codon deletion. Do not apply a single constant.

adaptive_but_deleterious_group_Y.note: completes the switch structurally but destabilises the AF-H network; lethal without X and Z
adaptive_but_deleterious_group_Y.human_GR_note: site 212 maps to GR 742 (+530), not 743; the deletion shifts the offset

permissive_group_Z.human_GR_note: GR 557 is Trp in human GR, not the Thr of AncGR2's N26T -- human GR has diverged further at this site. GR 636 matches Q105L.

receptor_versions.AncCR: Ancestral corticoid receptor, ~450 Ma, MR-like: responds to aldosterone, DOC and cortisol. Carries ancestral Tyr27.
receptor_versions.AncGR1: GR of the common ancestor of jawed vertebrates; still MR-like in sensitivity. Already carries Y27R. All combinatorial mutagenesis was done on this background.
receptor_versions.AncGR2: GR of the common ancestor of bony vertebrates; cortisol-specific. Carries X, Y and Z.
receptor_versions._intervals: AncCR -> AncGR1: 25 substitutions. AncGR1 -> AncGR2: 36 substitutions plus one single-codon deletion.
receptor_versions._human_GR: 7PRX carries the derived states at Anc 27, 29, 98, 105, 106 and 111 (Arg558, Met560, Ile629, Leu636, Pro637, Gln642) but not at 26. Human GR is not AncGR2; use it as a scaffold, not as the derived genotype.
